summary: Interpreted the corrected config-change receipt (7dbd521fd90f47a488f5248d1f6a21f5, exit 0, both cases passed): all four comparisons are complete and hold, so the child question's configuration half and its wedge are decided — with identical phantom premises the phantom removal committed in 0 ms (configuration five to four voters), the consistent-voter removal did not commit within 5001 ms, and the follow-up removal of the phantom was then refused with a 1000 ms enqueue timeout and never committed, meaning one blocked change also removes the operator's ability to issue further changes. The child account is recorded as explained / defect_claim asserted with both receipts cited and the protective side stated: the steps that would shrink the voter set onto the phantom group cannot commit, so the phantom grant cannot become authority over committed entries by configuration change in this history. This turn also opens an independent lead on the authority-transition axis, @q_transfer_message_replay: TimeoutNowRequest embeds only the RPC header (commands.go 205-208) and timeoutNow validates nothing (raft.go 2232-2239), while the flag it sets is what makes voters skip the known-leader rejection in requestVote. The new two-case probe (deliver one TimeoutNow payload, then the identical payload again to whoever became leader; control: a plain follower campaign with the same log claim) is requested, with four comparisons — first delivery moves leadership, the duplicate raises the term again, the control's plain vote is refused, and the control changes no leadership. Local construction runs show the predicted contrast (term 2 -> 3 on the first delivery, 3 -> 4 on the duplicate, while the control's vote was not granted and the term stayed 2), but only construction feedback was observed; the retained receipt, partitions during replay, larger clusters and the length of the leadership gap remain open.
